Of course. An exposure-wide scan requires specifying which family of chemicals to test. Once you select a category, I will run the analysis.

To address your second question—"how confident should we be?"—I will follow up the initial scan with a sensitivity analysis (`nhanes_sensitivity`) on the top results. This is a critical step for a phenotype like uric acid, as it helps disentangle whether the exposure is truly associated with the outcome or if the association is confounded by underlying health conditions.

Please choose one of the following exposure categories to scan:

*   `metals`
*   `persistent organic pollutants (POPs)`
*   `phytoestrogens`
*   `polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)`
*   `organochlorine pesticides (OCPs)`
*   `volatile organic compounds (VOCs)`
*   `polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs)`
*   `phenols`
*   `parabens`
*   `phthalates & plasticizers`
*   `all` (Note: this will take significantly longer, 20-30 minutes)
